terms.comment: Traupman’s chartulārum (lūsōriārum) lūdus, after his chartula lūsōria for the card itself (see playing card).
The ablative of the thing played with, as in pilā lūdere, tālīs lūdere (Cic. Sen. 58).

evidence: M-O s.v. card game, from Vives 1540
terms.comment: With chartīs lūdere, “play cards”: Vives’s words.

evidence: M-O s.v. card game, from Vives 1540
terms.comment: Vives’s other word, from folium lūsōrium, a playing card; with foliīs lūsitāre, “play cards”.

phrases.latin: Adfer, quaesō, folia lūsōria, quae inveniēs sub abacō ad sinistram.
phrases.english: Bring the playing cards, please: you’ll find them under the sideboard on the left.

sources: Lewis & Short: chartula · Lewis & Short: lusorius · Lewis & Short: folium
